text:
Alex: Heads-up, I'm starting onboarding for vendor-44b-opt. Weights uploaded to s3://redwood-models/vendor-44b-opt/v1 — initial smoke shows tokenization dropping leading spaces for some prompts and RoPE scale appears mismatched vs other 30/40b models. Can runtime + infra eyeball?

Maya: on it. do you have the model config you used?

Alex: pasted minimal payload below. ran local smoke with seq=2048.

```json
{
  "model_name": "vendor-44b-opt",
  "weights": "s3://redwood-models/vendor-44b-opt/v1/",
  "gqa": true,
  "mqa": "auto",
  "rope_scale": 1.0,
  "attn_impl": "cutlass-like"
}
```

Alex: command I ran: `python infra/tools/smoke.py --weights s3://redwood-models/vendor-44b-opt/v1/ --seq 2048 --batch 4`

Sam: quick Q — vendor says tokenizer is byte-level BPE but their export uses sentencepiece vocab.txt. that mismatch explains leading-space drop. did you try forcing the tokenizer mapping to our `byte_bpe` fallback?

Alex: haven't tried fallback yet. I can re-export with `--tokenizer-format byte_bpe` if that helps.

Chris: regarding RoPE, their implementation uses scaling factor baked into embeddings (rope_scaling=0.75) while our standard is 1.0 for 40B family. If we load with rope_scale=1.0 you'll see attention drift at long contexts.

Isha: for GQA/MQA: vendor set `gqa: true` and `mqa: auto` — our loader treats `auto` as enabled when weight sharding matches MQA layout. Can someone dump the weight shard manifest (`weights/manifest.json`) so we can confirm?

Alex: pasted manifest excerpt:```
{ "shards": ["vendor-44b-opt-00001.pt", "vendor-44b-opt-00002.pt"], "shard_dim": 0 }
```

Maya: that looks like GQA (shard_dim=0) — MQA=false probably. I think `mqa: auto` will not flip on. Sam/Chris can you confirm loader behavior?

Sam: confirmed — loader checks for per-head packing pattern. With `shard_dim=0` we treat as GQA. Set `mqa: false` in config to be explicit.

Chris: On attention impl: `cutlass-like` is fine on CUDA 12 nodes but causes slight perf/precision diff compared to our reference kernel for kv-cache updates. For canary, I suggest `attn_impl: reference` to isolate rope scaling + tokenizer issues.

Alex: noted. I'll update config to `rope_scale: 0.75`, `mqa: false`, and `attn_impl: reference`. Re-uploading config now, pushing to s3://redwood-models/vendor-44b-opt/v1/config.json.

Isha: also flag: tokenizer mapping loss causes prompt scoring mismatch in our eval harness. If you re-export tokenizer, run `tools/tokenizer_check.py --vocab s3://.../vocab.txt` — it'll show leading-space tokenization diffs.

Alex: ran tokenizer check, output shows `"> " vs "Ġ" style space tokens — vendor SP vs our byte bpe. Will re-export and attach new vocab.

infra-bot: canary-rule-check: dedicated-pool-40b has capacity for rolling canary tomorrow 10:00 PT.

Maya: after Alex updates config + tokenizer, I'll run a short canary in staging with `--seq 4096 --use-prefix-cache` to validate RoPE at long context. Anyone want to be on the post-mortem if we see degradation?

Sam: I'll join the canary window. I'll also open a small fast-lint PR to fail CI if `mqa` is `auto` and manifest indicates GQA.

Alex: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4321 — includes config change + tokenizer export. PTAL @Maya @Sam

Chris: quick code-review nit on the PR — please add an integration test that runs `smoke.py` with `attn_impl: reference` and asserts perplexity delta < 2% against baseline.

Alex: will add test. Also, for runtime folks: any concerns with enabling `use-prefix-cache` on this model? vendor suggests high context reuse for chat prompts.

Maya: prefix caching is fine, but TTL default 120s might evict frequently if concurrency high. We should set `cache_ttl_seconds: 600` for the canary to see real reuse effects.

Isha: logging note — add a token-level mismatch alert in console for this canary so we can catch tokenizer drift quickly (`alerts: [tokenizer-delta]`).

Alex: updated canary plan: rope_scale=0.75, mqa=false, attn_impl=reference, cache_ttl_seconds=600, tokenizer=re-exported byte_bpe. Canary scheduled 2025-06-04 10:00 PT on dedicated-pool-40b.

Maya: perfect. I'll run the long-context smoke and post results here.

Sam: I'll merge the lint PR after CI.

Chris: pinging eng-oncall if anything spikes. :bell:

Alex: thanks all — will follow up with a short results thread after canary. :thumbsup:
